body: Is there a reason `270` and `90` are inverted?
Can you validate the issue raised in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/98709 for the use of `windowManager.getDefaultDisplay().getRotation()` doesn't apply here as well.

Thanks for the review!

While Display.getRotation() can be unreliable for determining the *Vulkan rendering pre-transform*, it still reflects the *logical orientation of the display surface*.

Orienting camera images requires aligning the camera sensor with this *logical display orientation*. The standard calculation uses sensor orientation and the *display's rotation*, not the Vulkan swapchain transform (which is for *rendered output* transformation).

So, using Display.getRotation() (or equivalent logical display info) for camera orientation is the correct approach, separate from Vulkan rendering details.

Should `p_parameters` be used to update the selected format?
This logic is duplicated in the destructor, can you move it into an helper function and use that instead.

Linux supports setting several parameters.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/camera/camera_feed_linux.cpp#L257-L266

For macOS, `p_parameters` is not used since `set_format` is not overridden. Similarly, Android does not use `p_parameters` as there are no custom parameters.

We can't hardcode Meta specific stuff into the core.
